title: Enterprise Integration: Scale vs. Tight Coupling in Order Egress

steps.prompt: An enterprise ERP requires near-real-time updates when an Order or Account changes (450,000 events/day). Custom business payload transformation and filtering are required prior to external publication. Which integration pattern complies with Well-Architected Trust & Reliability?

options.label: Change Data Capture (CDC) custom channel with event enrichment configured on standard fields
options.distractorAntipattern: CDC custom channels only enrich unchanged record fields; they cannot execute procedural transformations, cross-object joins, or custom business payload formatting prior to egress.
options.rationale: While CDC custom channels support field enrichment, they cannot execute complex Apex transformations, join data from related objects, or apply conditional business filtering before event publishing.

options.label: High-Volume Platform Event published via an after-save trigger with custom enrichment
options.rationale: High-Volume Platform Events decouple downstream consumers asynchronously, allow Apex triggers to filter and reshape business payloads before publishing, and support 450k+ daily event volume.

options.label: Queueable Apex callout handler enqueued from the after-save trigger with backoff retries
options.distractorAntipattern: High-frequency Queueable callouts at 450,000 events/day exhaust rolling 24-hour asynchronous Apex allocations and create severe thread serialization bottlenecks.
options.rationale: At 450,000 events/day, firing individual Queueable Apex callouts exceeds standard asynchronous execution limits (250,000 daily or org allocation) and couples outbound delivery to external ERP availability.
